newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria's UDF to hold primaries before April vote.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria's UDF to hold primaries before April vote.

text.p: Bulgaria's opposition Union of Democratic Forces, the favourite to win general elections on April 19, will hold a U.S.-style primary election for representatives in the next parliament.
"People want trustworthy politicians and we will try to fill gaps in the current electoral law by holding internal primary elections," UDF deputy chairman Evgeni Bakardjiev told reporters.
Under Bulgaria's electoral law, adopted after the fall of communism seven years ago, a variable percentage of parliament seats is allocated on a proportional basis.
The law has frequently come under attack from voters, for letting corrupt officials slip onto national party lists and then into parliament.

In a two-day convention which ended on Sunday, the UDF decided to register as a single party and elected an 11-member National Executive Council, which replaced the previous supervising body, the Coordination Coucil.
"The Council is expected to work out a system for nominating candidates for parliament through primary elections," said UDF deputy Chairman Alexander Bozhkov.
The UDF, plagued by infighting in the past, said it will immediately negotiate election coalitions with its current partners the ethnic Turk Movement for Rights and Freedoms and the People's Union.
The anti-communist opposition held a U.S.-style primary election last year to select its presidential candidate, Petar Stoyanov, Bulgaria's current head of state.

The UDF emerged as favourite to win parliamentary polls after 30 days of mass protests fuelled by economic hardship forced the ruling Socialists to agree 12 days ago to early elections, 20 months before the end of their term.
Stoyanov last week appointed an interim caretaker cabinet.

On Saturday the UDF urged that the president's powers be strengthened to cope with the crisis facing the country and proposed setting up an anti-mafia body under presidential supervision to crack down on corruption, strengthen state institutions and crush organised crime.
Set up after the fall of the communist regime seven years ago, the UDF was a coalition of democratic, agrarian and monarchist parties.
It formed the first non-communist government after winning general elections in 1991, but surrendered power after 11 months in office, failing to win backing for radical reforms.

"The UDF's major tasks now are to win an outright majority in the elections and, together with all current opposition partners, lead Bulgaria out of its devastating crisis," said UDF chairman Ivan Kostov.
